output.brief:
The soft-pedal complaints almost certainly come from contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique, the Tessaro pads or the hills. Northfield Motor Services used a bulk drum of fluid that had gone without a cap and had taken on water. Two vans tested on 24 Sep had boiling points of 152°C and 149°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. All 11 complaint vans were serviced at Northfield, and the two Northfield vans serviced from a fresh drum had no complaints. Vans serviced at Calder Road, with the same pads, show no problem. The same drivers had no brake complaints in other vans on the same hills. Northfield warned Larkspur on 25 Sep and nobody replied.

What to do this week: pull the Northfield-serviced vans, test the fluid, and renew it from sealed stock. Start with the 11 bulk-drum vans. Do not discipline complainants or run retraining, because that would punish people who reported a real fault and would hide further reports. Don't reorder pads on this evidence. I'm fairly confident. The remaining gap is that I haven't seen test results for every van.
